decisive_items: a well‐defined, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 90 × 44 × 55 mm in the right labia majora tracking into the inguinal canal
The leading preoperative impression was a canal of Nuck hernia containing omental tissue
without erythema, lymphadenopathy, or signs of inflammation
response.rationale: R1 matches the painless, non-inflammatory inguinal-tracking mass and ultrasound tracking into the canal, directly supported by the stated operative impression. R3 is a low-prior soft-tissue possibility but lacks the anatomical track into the inguinal canal. R2 is contradicted by absence of inflammation and typical Bartholin cyst features.

rejected.why: Bartholin cyst typically involves cystic inflammation or pain; here the mass is solid, non-tender, and extends into the inguinal canal with no inflammatory signs.
Lipoma is a generic soft-tissue consideration, but the ultrasound shows tracking into the inguinal canal and the leading impression is a canal of Nuck hernia, making this less specific and likely.
